VBO:0201251.summary: Friendly and keen on a scent trail, the Small Swiss Hound brings a calm manner to tracking and a determined voice to hunting. It can work independently, searching and driving game with a melodious cry, while keeping a strong attachment to its handler. The breed was developed for Swiss enclosed hunting grounds, where smaller, shorter-legged hounds were preferred to the faster Swiss Hound.
VBO:0201251.shortDescription: A calm tracker with a melodious hunting cry, the Small Swiss Hound combines independent work with attachment to its handler.

sources.title: FCI Standard60 — Swiss Short-Legged Hound
sources.evidence: Actual utilization, history and temperament paragraphs read: independent giving-tongue hunt, steady scent, melodious cry, calm-to-lively friendly character, difficult terrain and wounded-game tracking. Smaller hounds developed for enclosed Swiss shoots where medium Swiss hounds too fast. Complete normative head/body/limbs/rough coat/intact tail read;2015 allows mixed colors.

sources.title: Schweizer Niederlaufhund und Dachsbracken Club — breed
sources.evidence: Actual breed paragraphs read: high handler attachment, independent solo search/flush/loud trail cry, calm temperament/fine nose for wounded game. Current2015 standard no longer prescribes separated color varieties; all colors may intercross and mixed colors permitted. Absolute never-aggressive/family suitability claims deliberately omitted.
